s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of upper gastrointestinal bleeding with epigastric pain
salient_findings: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration
key_facts: One-week history of epigastric pain and hematemesis
No significant medical or surgical history
Hemoglobin rose to 10 g/dL after transfusion
Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa
Well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass measuring 6×5 cm with fat attenuation

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of upper gastrointestinal bleeding with epigastric pain

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa, consistent with GIST presentation

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Submucosal lesion with ulceration, possible benign tumor

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation, suggestive of lipoma

shortlist.label: Peptic ulcer disease
shortlist.why_kept: Epigastric pain and hematemesis, with ulceration of the overlying mucosa

shortlist.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of upper gastrointestinal bleeding with epigastric pain, possible Dieulafoy's lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of a submucosal lesion in the gastric antrum with ulceration of the overlying mucosa and a well-defined, heterogeneous, pre-pyloric mass with fat attenuation on CT suggests a gastrointestinal stromal tumor, which can cause bleeding and have a variable appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: Lipomas are typically homogeneous and composed entirely of fat, which does not match the heterogeneous appearance on CT

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are rare in the stomach and usually have a more uniform appearance

rejected.label: Peptic ulcer disease
rejected.why: Peptic ulcer disease typically presents with multiple ulcers and a history of NSAID use or Helicobacter pylori infection, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Dieulafoy's lesion
rejected.why: Dieulafoy's lesion is a small, superficial ulceration with a visible vessel, which does not match the large, submucosal lesion described
